title: spec review: Claude fix rounds resume the executor's session on the same account: a fix round of a Claude-executed task resumes its recorded session with the fix delta, falling back to a fresh run when the session or account is unavailable
spec:
Goal T-1403, wave 2, plan label B8. Codex fix rounds reuse the thread (`codex exec resume`, executor.reply) and
send deltas only; Claude fix rounds today start a fresh `claude -p` with the full packet, re-reading the repo
every round (analysis 2026-10-01: fix rounds are 41% of execute runs).

U4 resolved (2026-10-01): each account is a separate CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (spawn.py:1-2, 1306; pool.toml
[[claude_accounts]] config_dir ~/.claude-a / ~/.claude-b), and `claude --resume <id>` reads sessions from that
directory, so a session resumes only on the account that created it.

Facts (goal/T-1403 at 92c1a98 plus T-1453 and T-1457 merged before this task; re-check line numbers):
- spawn.py:1513 run_worker(task_id, account_id=None, *, resume_task=None, resume_prompt=None, session_id=None);
  1541 t['_resume_session'] = session_id; run_claude (1296) adds `--resume <id>` when task['_resume_session']
  is set (1323-1324) with the normal allowlist; 1385-1387 store packet_meta.session_id on the task after a run;
  1755-1759 resume_worker(task, prompt, session_id) re-runs on worker_registry's recorded account.
- run_worker claims the task on acct and cuts the worktree with ensure_worktree (1603); with B7 a fix round's
  worktree is cut from the held task's branch, so the resumed session sees a different directory than its
  original worktree: the resume prompt must state the new worktree path and that the previous worktree is gone.
- executor._exhausted (executor.py:545-597) is where a Claude row dispatch reaches run_worker(t['id'],
  account_id=acct.id) in a thread (580-596); acct = pool.pick('execute') (557).
- Codex fix rounds: grep 'fix_round_for' and 'no_thread' in executor.py for the thread-resume decision and the
  pipeline.resume record {'mode': 'fresh'|'thread', 'reason'} that the daemon already shows; mirror that shape.
- A held task records its account in task['account'] (spawn.py:1604) and executor 'claude:<tier>' (1564).

Change:
1. executor.claude_resume_plan(fix_task, pool) -> {'mode': 'session', 'session_id', 'account', 'held_id'} or
   {'mode': 'fresh', 'reason'}: fix_task has constraints.fix_round_for; held = bus.get(that); session =
   held.packet_meta.session_id; held.executor starts with 'claude:'; held.account names an account that is not
   cooling and has headroom (pool.pick('execute') returns it, or pool exposes the account by id with
   headroom); otherwise fresh with reason one of no_fix_round_for, no_session, not_claude, account_unavailable.
   Pure except for bus.get and pool reads.
2. _exhausted(): for a fix-round task on a Claude row, plan = claude_resume_plan(t, pool); mode session ->
   run_worker(t['id'], account_id=plan['account'], session_id=plan['session_id'], resume_task=t,
   resume_prompt=<fix delta>) where the fix delta is the fix round's own spec (already rendered by the daemon
   from fix-round.md) prefixed with one line: 'Resumed session for fix round <n>; work now in <new worktree
   path> on branch task/<id>; the previous worktree is gone; commit before the final message.' Record
   bus.update(t['id'], pipeline={..., 'resume': plan}) before the run (same key as the Codex record). mode fresh
   -> today's path plus the same pipeline.resume record.
3. spawn.run_worker with resume_task/resume_prompt: the packet is NOT re-rendered; the prompt is the resume
   prompt alone (confirm at 1541-1600 and fix it if the packet is still prepended); budget and timeout come
   from the fix task's constraints as today; the run logs through bus.log_run with resume='session' so the
   scorecard can compare fix-round cost by mode.
4. Fallback inside the run: when run_claude on a resumed session fails before any output with a message
   containing 'No conversation found' or 'session' and 'not found' (the CLI's error for an unknown session),
   run once more fresh (same account) and set pipeline.resume = {'mode': 'fresh', 'reason':
   'session_missing'}; one retry only.

Tests that assert the old behaviour (SPEC RULE): tests/test_executor.py fallback/dispatch tests (grep
'run_worker' and 'fix_round_for') patch run_worker and assert its kwargs: update the fix-round ones for the new
kwargs; tests/test_spawn.py resume tests (grep 'resume_task' / '_resume_session'). Run tests/test_executor.py and
tests/test_spawn.py.

Depends on B7 (spawn.py chain) and B2a T-1504 (executor.py: _exhausted's no-codex-row branch and the bounded requeue land there first; place the resume plan in the Claude-row dispatch path after them). Out of scope: daemon.py, merge.py,
pool.py (use existing accessors), prompts.

Work on the task branch cut from goal/T-1403. Commit first, then run the focused tests in the foreground; never
background a command and never run the full gate. Write tests as unittest.TestCase methods using tests/_harness.py
like the neighbouring tests.

Re-filed 2026-10-01 (replaces T-1459): depends_on re-pointed to T-1472, T-1467 after the B2v3/B4v3 respecs; the spec, acceptance and scope are unchanged.

Re-filed 2026-10-02 (replaces T-1476): depends_on re-pointed to T-1494, T-1488 after the round-3 respecs (B2v4, B4a/B4b, E12v3); spec, acceptance and scope unchanged.

Re-filed 2026-10-02 00:50 (replaces T-1498): B2 was split into B2a T-1504 (executor/pool/capacity) and B2b T-1506 (daemon.py); depends_on re-pointed to T-1494 and T-1504 because this task edits executor.py and spawn.py only; acceptance and scope unchanged.
acceptance: tests/test_executor.py::test_claude_fix_round_resumes_session_on_same_account: passes: with a held task (executor claude:sonnet, account A, packet_meta.session_id S) and its fix round dispatched to a Claude row, _exhausted calls run_worker with account_id 'A', session_id S and a resume_prompt that names the new worktree and branch, and records pipeline.resume {'mode': 'session', 'session_id': S, 'account': 'A', 'held_id': ...}; with no session_id, a non-Claude executor, or account A cooling, it calls run_worker fresh and records mode 'fresh' with the matching reason

tests/test_spawn.py::test_resumed_fix_round_uses_delta_prompt_and_retries_fresh_on_missing_session: passes: run_worker with resume_task/resume_prompt/session_id passes `--resume S` and the resume prompt (not a re-rendered packet) to the CLI, logs the run with resume 'session'; when the first run fails with 'No conversation found' it runs once more without --resume and sets pipeline.resume mode 'fresh' reason 'session_missing'

risks.issue: The existing resume branch of run_worker (1584-1589) reads worker_registry.get(task_id) and then recorded['model'] and recorded['tools']. It was written for resume_worker, where the same task already has a registry entry. A fix round is a new task id with no registry entry, so recorded is None and the call raises TypeError. Item 3 says 'confirm and fix', but the real gap is where model, tools and disclosure mode come from. They must come from the fix task's tier and TOOLS['execute'], not from the held task's record.

Claude Code stores sessions per project directory, keyed by cwd. B7 cuts the fix round into a new worktree, so `claude --resume S` from that cwd will probably not find S, and the fallback would fire on every resume. U4 only settled the config-dir question, not the cwd question. The acceptance tests mock the CLI, so they cannot catch this. The spec also asks the resume prompt to name the new worktree path, but the worktree is only cut at line 1648, after the prompt would have to be built.

Both `resume_task is None` guards (1766 and 1831) switch off derived-result handling and execute_incomplete handling when resume_task is set. Passing resume_task=t for a fix round silently disables that safety net for exactly the rounds this feature targets. In run_claude, resume_session also silences log_run, which is a different mechanism from task['_resume_session']. The spec doesn't say which path is used or how resume='session' gets logged.

The fresh retry for a missing session is underspecified. run_worker with resume_task set never renders the packet, so a retry from inside that path has no full packet to send. The retry has to leave the resume branch and run the normal render path. If run_claude logs the failed first attempt and then the retry, cost and run counts are double counted. The failure detection on the CLI error string ('No conversation found', or 'session' plus 'not found') is also unguarded against matching ordinary model output; it should match only on the error result with no prior output.

The spec says to mirror the Codex pipeline.resume record with modes 'fresh'|'thread'. The real function is resume_plan(parent, fix_task) at line 320, and it returns {'mode': 'fresh'|'resume', 'reason'}. Its 'resume' mode is the Codex thread mode, and the daemon already reads this key. Writing 'session' under the same key may be misread, and a plain bus.update(pipeline=...) overwrites the whole pipeline dict unless the spec says to merge into the existing one.

Item 1 allows 'pool.pick("execute") returns it' as the account check, and item 2 then calls run_worker with account_id=plan['account'], which may differ from the acct that _exhausted already picked and capacity-checked. The B2a claude_row_free and bounded requeue accounting then no longer match the account that runs. The spec also doesn't say what happens when account A is free but the row's own capacity says to wait. It should name exactly one accessor (Pool.claude_has_headroom from B2a) and say the dispatch path keeps its own acct for the fresh case.

suggested_spec_changes: Specify where model, allowlist and disclosure mode come from in the resume branch (fix task tier, TOOLS['execute'], pool.cfg['models']) and remove the dependency on worker_registry.get(fix_task_id). Say what resume_worker keeps doing for same-task resumes.

Decide and verify the cwd issue before coding. Either run the resume from the held task's original worktree path (if it still exists), or add a cheap explicit check or one-time probe that a session is resumable from the new cwd. If it isn't, drop the feature or have the plan return 'fresh' with reason 'worktree_moved'. Add that reason to the enum.
Call ensure_worktree first, then build the resume prompt with the real path. Say that the 'previous worktree is gone' line is only emitted when the path really differs.

Introduce a dedicated flag (for example a task['_session_resume'] marker) instead of reusing resume_task. That way the derive_execute_result and execute_incomplete guards, the packet_meta recording and the log_run path stay on for fix rounds. Define how the fresh retry re-enters the normal render path with the same account.

Log only one run per attempt, and give the failed resume attempt an outcome such as 'resume_failed' and no cost. Detect 'session_missing' only when the CLI returned an error result with no assistant output.

Use pipeline.resume with the existing key semantics. Merge into the current pipeline dict. Either reuse mode 'resume' with a provider field, or add 'session' and confirm that daemon readers tolerate it. If the daemon needs a change, say so. daemon.py is out of scope.
Name one account-headroom accessor (Pool.claude_has_headroom from B2a) and say that a fresh fallback uses the acct that _exhausted already picked.

Say that the resumed run's session_id replaces packet_meta.session_id on the fix task. Add acceptance covering model, tools and budget on the resumed run, a single log_run per attempt, and the retry not double counting.
Add a rollback note: a pool.toml or config flag, off by default, that forces mode 'fresh' with reason 'disabled'. Without one, the only revert is git revert.
